items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like mergeConsistentHash, unionConsistentHashIR and ConsistentHashCookieAttribute say what they do. Doc comments are on all new API types and fields, and the code follows the same layout as the other trafficpolicy features.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The code follows the plugin pattern: types, constructConsistentHash in constructor.go, applyConsistentHash, and mergeConsistentHash registered in mergeFuncs. Build and merge share the union/clone helpers, merge uses SetOne/Append, and deepcopy/CRD files are generated.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: constructConsistentHash returns errors that are added to the errors slice, and Validate is registered. CEL rules plus MinLength=1 check input. The merge clones p2's IR instead of sharing it, and an unsupported strategy logs a warning like the other merge functions do.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. It calls unionConsistentHashIR with the higher-priority policy first, which dedupes, re-sorts into canonical order and keeps the higher-priority sourceIp. It respects disable, records "consistentHash" via Append/SetOne, and the tests check sourceIp retention and origins.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The ApplyForRoute test turns {} into a single sourceIp policy with terminal=false. In the merge, disable suppresses broader policies. The XValidation rule "when disable is true, no other fields may be set" is on the ConsistentHash type and is generated into the CRD.
